newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia will not join Paris Club by G7 meeting.
newsitem.headline: Russia will not join Paris Club by G7 meeting.

text.p: Russia will not be given membership in the Paris Club of creditor countries during the Group of Seven industrialised nations meeting in Denver, a senior Finance Ministry official said on Monday.
"Russia will not enter the Paris Club before Denver," First Deputy Finance Minister Alexei Kudrin told Reuters.
"The talks are not at the stage where the issue can be finally solved. Denver could give a preliminary political evaluation of our work."

A Finance Ministry official said earlier that Russia would decide whether or not to join the Paris Club by the G7 meeting, which has been dubbed G8 because Russia, not formally a G7 member, will attend.

"Russia does not agree with the terms offered to us by the Paris Club at first," Kudrin said. "It is connected to the credits granted by Russia, including the ones of military-technical nature. I think in Denver we shall discuss the main terms (of our joining the Club)."
Russia is seeking repayment of $37 billion owed to it by debtor countries which have agreements with the Club.
First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said recently Russia would try to speed up payments from Libya and Iraq.
Kudrin said the government was working on a programme to boost debt repayments to Russia over 1997-98.

As part of the programme the Finance Ministry recently revised proceeds from debt repayments in 1997, increasing the volume to $1.5 billion from an initial $1 billion and it can raise the figure further, he said.
